title: Greedy

views.title: Greedy
views.intro: Greedy is right when an exchange argument or a "stays ahead" invariant holds. State the argument in one sentence before coding; if you cannot, think DP. Typical shapes: furthest reach, sort by a key, two passes, ratio ordering, heap of options.
table: Candy, gas station style prefix logic

files.desc: Jump game I/II, gas station, candy, partition labels, queue reconstruction, cookies, largest number, units, valid parenthesis string, boats, refueling, straights, lemonade

pitfalls: Without a proof sketch, test the greedy against brute force on small inputs.
Largest Number: compare a+b with b+a, and special-case an all-zero result.
Valid Parenthesis String: carry a range [lo, hi] of possible open counts, not a single count.

views.title: Greedy: Exchange & Construction
views.intro: Most hard greedy problems are one of: sort by a derived key, construct digit by digit, repair a violation locally, or work backwards. If you cannot state the exchange argument, prove it on a tiny case first.
table: Operations that are easier to undo than to do
Largest number by one swap / merge
Make array non-decreasing with one change

files.desc: Remove duplicate letters, wiggle subsequence, two-city scheduling, bag of tokens, broken calculator, monotone increasing digits, split array into consecutive subsequences, maximum swap, non-decreasing array, advantage shuffle, fractional knapsack, domino rotations, create maximum number, min add to make valid, min operations to form a target, longest pair chain

pitfalls: Greedy without a proof fails on a counterexample; test the rule on 3-4 element inputs.
Work-backwards problems: divide or subtract from the target instead of multiplying from the start.
Sort stability and ties matter when the derived key can be equal.

decisions.q: Can you reach the end / minimum jumps?
Need the best past option when stuck?
Smallest lexicographic subsequence using each letter once?
Assign people to two groups minimizing total cost?
Forward moves branch a lot, reverse moves are forced?

decisions.a: Last-occurrence table, swap with the best later digit

decisions.q: Merge two digit sequences into the maximum number?
decisions.a: Best subsequence per length, merge by suffix comparison

calibration: SDE2 bar: jump game I/II, gas station, assign cookies, best time to buy and sell II, merge intervals.
SDE3 bar: candy, queue reconstruction, partition labels, largest number, task scheduler, valid parenthesis string, with a stated exchange argument.
Staff bar (for context): proving optimality or finding a counterexample fast, matroid-style greedy, and recognizing when greedy gives a good approximation but not an exact answer.
Staff bar: justify each greedy with an exchange argument out loud; digit-construction problems (maximum number, remove duplicate letters) are the common hard ones.
